method: Fix size from the eight-print base rate, scaled up for the current vol regime. For direction, weigh only two things: a persistent asymmetric reaction record (a name that repeatedly guides down), and whether the run-in has already reset expectations. Legible preview sentiment and peer beats are discounted as priced. Neutral unless both directional inputs point the same way.
key_drivers: Six of the last seven bmo prints produced negative reactions (-3.4 to -14.6%); structural guide-down pattern
Realised 20d vol 76% annualised implies an outsized event move regardless of sign
Down 18.1% in a month vs semicap group -12.7%: relative underperformance partly resets the bar
Peers FormFactor/Teradyne beat strongly, so a sector-wide low bar is already legible and priced
Preview notes ENTG has missed revenue estimates repeatedly over two years
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the -18% month already discounted a second-half guidance cut, which would flip the washed-out positioning into the dominant force.
reasoning: The one durable directional fact is the reaction record: ENTG sells off on its own prints even in decent tape, six of seven. Against that, a 13.8% twenty-day drawdown into the print lowers the bar and peers reported well. I keep a modest downward tilt rather than a strong one. Size is the confident part: 76% realised vol against a 5.6% median historical move argues for roughly 8%.

method: Fix size from the eight-print base rate. For direction, weigh which part of the release is already known versus still open, and how much optimism the run-in has already banked. A pre-released revenue line narrows the upside channel and leaves margin and guidance as the live variables. Discount preview sentiment as priced.
key_drivers: Q2 net sales pre-released on 22 July: $341m, only +2% y/y, Europe -4%, with a 3% Middle East war headwind
Stock sits exactly at its 52-week high and at/above the $125.80 average analyst target on that lukewarm sales print
Revenue is de-risked, so only EPS, gross margin and full-year guidance remain live - and last quarter had a significant gross margin miss
Counterweight: six of eight prior reactions positive, median move only 1.95%, and the pre-release structure is routine rather than new
Pre-released sales compress the event move; 30.9% vol argues for roughly 3%
what_would_change_my_mind: A full-year guidance raise alongside recovered gross margin, which would justify the 52-week high and invert the asymmetry I am pricing.
reasoning: The 22 July 8-K is the hard-won item here: sales are already public and unimpressive, yet the stock closed at a 52-week high above the consensus target. That leaves margin and guidance as the only surprise channels, and the flagged Middle East headwind, European softness and last quarter's gross margin miss all skew that channel down. I hold the tilt modest because IPAR pre-releases every quarter and still reacted positively six of eight times, so the structure alone is not an edge.
